subject.title: [Feature]: LLM distillation/extraction gate for memory-core deep-phase promotion (distill, don't dump raw snippets into MEMORY.md)

question: Should memory-core deep promotion add an opt-in model-backed distillation step before writing MEMORY.md, or should deterministic snippet capping remain the accepted promotion behavior for now?
rationale: The request changes durable memory semantics and adds likely config/model fallback policy; source inspection shows no missing narrow bug fix to apply without maintainer direction.

options.title: Design the distillation gate first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define opt-in config, fallback, safety, and test expectations before any implementation PR.

options.title: Decline model-backed promotion
options.body: Close or mark not planned if maintainers want MEMORY.md promotion to stay deterministic and avoid model-generated durable facts.

options.title: Queue a scoped implementation after approval
options.body: Once direction is explicit, a PR can add the gate in memory-core with docs, schema, and regression coverage.

recommendation.title: Design the distillation gate first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define opt-in config, fallback, safety, and test expectations before any implementation PR.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory-core state migration work and repository config policy make this the best available product-direction routing signal.
